data.narrative:
Mission Zero Technologies is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Nicholas Chadwick, Shiladitya Ghosh, and Gaël Gobaille-Shaw, having raised £21.8M to date. The valuation exercise draws on a comp universe of nine frontier-tech peers in Climate & Energy—one public (LNZA) and eight private, including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

The stage-progression method is applicable and anchors the analysis. Using total capital raised (£21.8M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage transitions yields an implied valuation of £44M. A peer-median approach is not applicable; while eight same-sector peers exist, none meet minimum comparability thresholds (three or more datapoints) when filtered for same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier. Deploying all-sector medians would introduce excessive noise.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of £37M to £50M, with a median of £44M. This range reflects the stage-progression method applied to the capital-raised baseline, with bounds accounting for typical variance in step-up multiples and early-stage discount factors. Key uncertainties include the absence of narrow-set peer comps, limiting cross-validation, and the inherent sensitivity of frontier-tech valuations to technology risk and market-adoption assumptions not captured in capital-flow metrics alone.
